questions.title: Can the research substrate itself evolve?
questions.description: With model, budget, Lean toolchain, verifier, provenance boundary, and holdout tasks fixed, can the substrate around a group of agents learn which objects to store, how to link them, and when to make them inheritable?

questions.title: What is the smallest trustworthy feedback loop?
questions.description: Can a mathematical agent inspect the exact local state produced by an action, test the relevant consequence, and preserve the result so that another agent can continue?

questions.title: How should unfinished mathematical work be represented?
questions.description: Which distinctions matter for continuation: active routes, valid certificates, unresolved obligations, failed branches, or the provenance of a claim?

questions.title: When does persistent state become inherited research rather than a larger context window?
questions.description: Can a later agent inherit a versioned state, understand what is provisional, and make a new contribution without silently treating retrieval as proof?

questions.title: What does replaceability require?
questions.description: Can an agent, maintainer, verifier, or runtime component be replaced at a stated level without invalidating the evidence?

questions.title: How can a research organization learn without flattening its evidence?
questions.description: How should a central map preserve differences between code, tests, computed results, formal proof, and open conjecture while recording failures that change the direction?

questions.title: What should remain after a shared experience ends?
questions.description: What can remain returnable, interpretable, and alive after an immediate shared experience ends?
